name: Hirschsprung Disease-Nail Hypoplasia-Dysmorphism Syndrome
aliases: Hirschsprung Disease with Nail Hypoplasia and Dysmorphic Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hirschsprung Disease-Nail Hypoplasia-Dysmorphism Syndrome

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of intestinal aganglionosis consistent with Hirschsprung disease
Presence of hypoplastic or absent fingernails and/or toenails
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance
Mild to moderate developmental delay or intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of intestinal aganglionosis, nail hypoplasia, and characteristic dysmorphic facial features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intestinal aganglionosis causing functional bowel obstruction
searchTerms: missing nerve cells in intestines causing blockage
intestinal nerve absence leading to obstruction
bowel blockage from lack of intestinal nerves

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplastic or absent fingernails and toenails
searchTerms: absent nails on fingers and toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, micrognathia)
searchTerms: wide-set eyes and broad nose bridge
small lower jaw with facial differences
distinct facial features with spaced eyes

common.symptomName: Chronic constipation or intestinal obstruction in neonatal period
searchTerms: chronic constipation or blockage in newborns

laboratory: Histopathology showing absence of enteric ganglion cells in affected bowel segments
Normal routine blood tests unless complications arise
imaging: Contrast enema demonstrating transition zone in colon
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern suggested by family history
other: Physical examination revealing nail hypoplasia and characteristic facial dysmorphism

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of nail hypoplasia and dysmorphic features
Isolated intestinal aganglionosis without systemic anomalies
Presence of nail dysplasia with patellar hypoplasia
Hirschsprung disease with distinctive facial features
Genetic testing positive for ZEB2 mutations

redFlags: Neonatal intestinal obstruction with failure to pass meconium
Progressive developmental delay or neurological deterioration
references: Am J Med Genet. 1998;77(3):233-237. Clinical and genetic aspects of Hirschsprung disease with nail hypoplasia
